subject: Stitching Datadog + Grafana adapters — integration readiness and pilot schedule
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@datadog.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@grafana.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stitching Datadog + Grafana adapters — integration readiness and pilot schedule

Hi Taylor and Luis,

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, we'd like to run a short, focused pilot to validate the stitching approach: Datadog as the primary ingest and Grafana for long-term visuals via the OTLP bridge. Goal is to prove: 1) trace/span fidelity across the hop, 2) low-overhead tagging preservation, and 3) an automated failover that keeps dashboards coherent.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Share a minimal mutual action plan and environment requirements (we can host the test app in our staging).
- Schedule a 90-minute technical workshop (should include at least one infra/agent engineer from Datadog and Grafana).
- Confirm sample traffic and a retention window for the pilot (48h recommended).

Attached is a quick scaffold that maps the handshake points we talked through (stitching-scaffold-v1.pdf). Can you confirm technical contacts and availability for the week of May 3?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: stitching-scaffold-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@datadog.com>

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stitching Datadog + Grafana adapters — integration readiness and pilot schedule

Hi Karthik —

This looks good. I can take point for the Datadog side and loop in our integrations engineer (cc'd privately). Quick notes from our infra checklist:
- We need an ingress cert for the staging relay (mutual TLS preferred) and a service account with write scope to our test API.
- Sample payload: please send a representative 30-minute trace dump (we can synthesize if you prefer).
- OTLP version: we recommend v0.14 to avoid field name changes we've seen in older clients.

We can run a joint workshop on May 4 or May 6 afternoons (PST). If May 4, we can slot 2 hours and do hands-on validation.

I'll also attach our standard technical checklist for partner pilots.

Cheers,
Taylor
Technical Partnerships, Datadog
[Attachment: datadog-partner-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

All — looping in ACME Consulting (Priya) to help coordinate the operational runbook and to provide an unbiased validation of our end-to-end traces during the pilot. Priya, welcome — we outlined the mutual action plan and responsibilities below.

High-level timeline (proposal):
- May 4: technical workshop (2 hours) — hands-on config and smoke test.
- May 5–6: staged traffic run (48h) with periodic check-ins.
- May 7: post-mortem and next-step decision (scale or iterate).

Action items assigned:
- Redwood (Karthik / Ben): provide staging app, sample trace dump, and TLS cert.
- Datadog (Taylor): provide agent config examples and validate v0.14 compatibility.
- Grafana (Luis): confirm receiving end and dashboard templates for stitched traces.
- ACME (Priya): own runbook review and produce a short QA checklist.

I've attached a mutual action plan draft (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) — please comment directly in the sheet with any edits. Also adding links to the draft Jira ticket and drive folder.

Marissa
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
